title: Hazel and the Letter
premise: In the river town of Vellum's Reach, Xanthe Crane has spent three years quietly finishing the great atlas his master died protecting — an atlas whose margins hide a coded ledger of names belonging to a persecuted border people. When the army requisitions the town and demands the master's papers, Xanthe must decide whether to surrender the atlas or honor a peacetime promise to Sefa, the cartographer's daughter now declared an enemy of the crown. Hunted by Captain Aldous Vane, who wants the ledger to destroy the community and claim its lands, Xanthe smuggles the names out through the very maps meant to chart them. In the end he trades the finished atlas itself for Sefa's escape, keeping only one hand-drawn page — proof that what is inherited is not property but obligation.
about_author: M. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated documents in provincial record offices. Hartwell writes historical fiction about the quiet people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlived Him
chapters.summary: Xanthe Crane, POV. Three years after Master Ellery's death, Xanthe inks the final coastline of the atlas in the locked workshop above the map shop, keeping his head down as soldiers drill in the square below. He touches the sealed margin-cases Ellery forbade him to open. Emotional beat: dutiful grief, the comfort of busy hands over an unspoken promise.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Captain Aldous Vane arrives with a requisition order: all maps, ledgers, and correspondence in the town are crown property, effective immediately. The town clerk hands over lists of residents, including the atlas workshop. Xanthe hides the margin-cases inside a rolled wall map. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: years earlier, Ellery made Xanthe swear that if anything happened, the ledger of names would reach Sefa, his estranged daughter across the border. Present-day Xanthe learns Sefa's people have been declared enemy and her name appears on Vane's arrest list. Emotional beat: the weight of a promise becoming dangerous.

chapters.title: The Names in the Margins
chapters.summary: Xanthe finally opens the margin-cases and deciphers Ellery's cipher: hundreds of names of the border folk, hidden in map annotations, evidence that could save them from dispossession — or condemn them if Vane reads it first. His apprentice friend Tamsin helps him copy pages. Emotional beat: awe and terror at inheriting a secret.

chapters.title: The Captain's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. The captain inspects the workshop, charming and precise, and notices the atlas is unfinished — one coastline blank. He gives Xanthe three days to complete it, calling it a courtesy. Xanthe understands it is a trap: finish the map, deliver the secrets inside it. Emotional beat: polite menace.

chapters.title: What Belongs to Whom
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. The army seizes homes along the river; neighbors who once ignored the workshop now beg Xanthe for copies of their own boundary lines. Belonging proves to be paper-thin. Tamsin urges him to burn the ledger and run. Emotional beat: guilt — his safety was always bought with others' erasure.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Fee
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Xanthe seeks out Old Brannoc, a ferryman who once carried Ellery's letters north, and bargains for passage to the border. Brannoc warns the crossings are watched since the declaration. First payment: a map of the marsh channels no soldier owns. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, transactional trust.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Going through Ellery's seized correspondence, Vane finds a letter hinting at 'the inheritance' and realizes the atlas contains more than geography. He begins cross-referencing the town's requisitioned ledgers against the map's marginalia. Emotional beat: the corrupt thrill of a hunt justified as duty.

chapters.title: Three Days of Ink
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Working day and night under guard, Xanthe completes the atlas beautifully — while altering two coordinates so the army's survey will misplace a village by a mile. Tamsin covers for him at the risk of her own name. Emotional beat: craftsmanship as resistance.

chapters.title: The Blank Coastline
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Vane presents the finished atlas to his superiors and discovers the altered coordinate when a scouting party reports wrong terrain. Someone in the workshop is working against him. He narrows the suspects to Xanthe. Emotional beat: wounded pride curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Arrests on Copper Lane
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Soldiers drag families from Copper Lane using the very boundary maps Xanthe drew. A boy Xanthe taught to read compasses is taken. Xanthe realizes every day he delays, the ledger's names become prisoners. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into urgency.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Tamsin is offered immunity to report on Xanthe. She stalls, then secretly moves half the copied names to the dye-house where she works, hiding them in bolt cloth bound for market towns. Emotional beat: courage discovered in an ordinary person.

chapters.title: The Marsh at Night
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. First escape attempt: Xanthe and Brannoc ferry the margin-cases upriver by night, but a patrol lantern forces them to sink the cases in a reed bed marked only on Xanthe's memory-map. Emotional beat: terror, loss, and the strange freedom of carrying nothing.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Vane arrests Tamsin and questions her gently, offering her future instead of pain. She gives him nothing but a forged inventory. Vane, humiliated before his superiors, decides to make an example — and to use Xanthe's promise against him by announcing Sefa's capture. Emotional beat: cruelty dressed as procedure.

chapters.title: The Lie About Sefa
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Proclamation: Sefa has been taken at the border crossing. Xanthe knows it may be bait, but cannot gamble her life on his caution. He walks into the garrison voluntarily, offering the atlas's location in exchange for her release. Emotional beat: love overriding strategy.

chapters.title: Bargaining With a Mapmaker's Ghost
chapters.summary: Vane and Xanthe, alternating. In the garrison office, Xanthe offers the true atlas; Vane reveals Sefa was never captured — the proclamation was a test, and Xanthe failed it by coming. But Xanthe counters: the atlas Vane holds is already worthless without the cipher key, which exists only in Xanthe's head. Stalemate. Emotional beat: two men discovering they need each other's ruin.

chapters.title: The Reed Bed at Low Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Under escort to retrieve the sunken cases, Xanthe leads the soldiers into the marsh and uses his own channel-maps to lose them in fog, escaping with the ledger while the patrol founders. Brannoc waits at the far bank. Emotional beat: the hunted turning hunter, mastery of place as power.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Was For
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. At a safehouse, Xanthe meets the border community's elders and understands at last why Ellery made the atlas: not to record land, but to prove the people's tenure upon it. They ask him to finish the work — to put their names back on the map openly. Emotional beat: belonging found, inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: The Trade at the Border Stone
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe, POV. Vane, facing disgrace, pursues to the border stone where Sefa waits with the community. Xanthe offers the completed atlas — the masterpiece, his master's life's work — in exchange for Vane withdrawing the requisition and releasing Tamsin and the prisoners. Vane, needing a trophy more than names he can no longer read, accepts. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the corrupt man's hunger for appearance over substance.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Released, Tamsin returns to a town half-emptied but stirring; the returned prisoners tell of the mapmaker's apprentice who traded everything. Vane files the atlas away unread, its marginalia meaningless to him — power holding paper instead of people. Emotional beat: bitter, hard-won relief.

chapters.title: The Page I Kept
chapters.summary: Xanthe, POV. Across the border, Xanthe begins teaching the community's children to draw their own maps, their own names at the center. He keeps one page from the old atlas: Ellery's first sketch, with both their names in the corner. Emotional beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Letter
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Years later, Sefa — called Hazel by the children for her eyes — receives a letter containing a single pressed leaf and a new map of the valley, every family named. She writes back to the apprentice who became a mapmaker of people. Emotional beat: quiet fulfillment; inheritance passed on, promise kept.
